# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Requests to /search blocked by SQLi managed rule group
**Description:** Two `GET /search` requests from IP 3.112.151.5 (JP) were BLOCKed (403) by `AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet` (rule SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS), while 35 `/page/N` requests from the same IP were ALLOWed. The two blocked query strings were `q=credit UNION members SELECT best savings plan` (03:58:52Z) and `q=our UNION workers SELECT new leadership` (03:58:58Z) — benign free-text searches, not attacks.
**Time:** 2026-09-08T03:58:52Z - 2026-09-08T03:58:58Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: SQLi managed rule keyword-matches benign /search text (SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS, LOW sensitivity, ALL_QUERY_ARGS)
**Description:** The `SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS` sub-rule of `AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet` returns BLOCK (403) because the `q` search parameter contains the token pair `UNION`…`SELECT`. Both blocked searches are ordinary English — "credit union members select best savings plan" and "our union workers select new leadership" — with no SQL syntax at all (no quotes, comments `--`/`#`, operators like `OR 1=1`, parentheses, or `FROM`/table structure). The same client (3.112.151.5, JP, desktop Chrome/HTTP2) browsed `/page/1`…`/page/35` normally and the rate-based rules never fired (~37 requests, well under the 500/5min limit). The rule is working as configured but is mis-tuned for a free-text search endpoint: keyword-only matching by the AWS managed SQLi signature on benign natural-language `/search` query text is the fundamental cause. A targeted WAF tuning on the `/search` endpoint (scope-down or override SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS to Count for that path) prevents recurrence. WebACL: `[redacted ARN]`.
**Cascades to:** symptom-sqli-block

#### Supporting Observations
- **Blocked /search queries are benign natural-language searches:** Full match detail for the two blocked `GET /search` requests from IP 3.112.151.5 shows both are **false positives** — ordinary free-text search phrases that happen to contain the English words 'UNION' and 'SELECT'.

- **03:58:52Z** — `q=credit UNION members SELECT best savings plan` → matched tokens [credit, UNION, members, SELECT, best]
- **03:58:58Z** — `q=our UNION workers SELECT new leadership` → matched tokens [our, UNION, workers, SELECT, new]

Terminating rule: **SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS** (AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet), sensitivitylevel **LOW**, location **ALL_QUERY_ARGS**, label `awswaf:managed:aws:sql-database:SQLi_QueryArguments`. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Apply a path-scoped SQLi tuning to the CloudFront WebACL `response-id-on-page` so the `SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS` sub-rule is relaxed to Count ONLY on `/search`, while full-strength BLOCK SQLi protection is preserved on every other path and for every other SQLi sub-rule on `/search`.

## Reasoning
The two 403s on GET /search (2026-09-08 03:58:52 and 03:58:58 UTC) were a confirmed false positive: the SQLi_QUERYARGUMENTS sub-rule of AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet (Priority 300) matched the keyword pair UNION…SELECT inside benign natural-language searches (`q=credit UNION members SELECT best savings plan`, `q=our UNION workers SELECT new leadership`), with no SQL syntax. SQLi sensitivity is already LOW and cannot be lowered. This change relaxes only the query-arguments sub-rule and only on /search via a split-group approach — the narrowest viable scope. A bare RuleActionOverride would relax it site-wide; a group-level scope-down excluding /search would disable ALL SQLi sub-rules on /search. Tradeoff: SQLi patterns in query arguments on /search are counted, not blocked (other SQLi sub-rules and KnownBadInputs at Priority 301 still apply).
